papers.title: An Asset Administration Shell-Based Digital Product Passport as a Gaia-X Service
papers.key_contribution: Stack: AAS submodels exposed over REST, planned as a Gaia-X service for decentralised exchange and storage. Data model covers lifecycle data used for product carbon footprint and remanufacturing; to be set up as demonstrators in a learning factory. The abstract reports no measured evaluation.
papers.conformance_relevance: Submodel structure maps to aas.validate (file level) and, if the AAS REST contract is pinned, to api.contract. The Gaia-X service layer (identity, self-description) has no existing check; it would need a mock trust and catalogue fixture on loopback, never a live Gaia-X node.

papers.title: A Multi-Stakeholder Digital Product Passport Based on the Asset Administration Shell
papers.venue: 2023 IEEE 28th International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA)
papers.key_contribution: Stack: cloud platform where each stakeholder builds its own AAS from templates through a user interface, with role-based access constraints and room for third-party services. Demonstrated on a real recycling use case; limitations are not stated in the abstract.
papers.conformance_relevance: Role-based visibility is the target of access.restricted_fields, but that check reads entitled paths at the root of the fetch body; element-level rules inside nested AAS submodels would need nested path support (gap). The generated AAS files fit aas.validate. Write operations by many parties are outside a passive engine; persistence.versions could observe their effect.

papers.title: Generate Digital Product Passports by Integrating Production Data into the Asset Administration Shell
papers.venue: 2024 IEEE 29th International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA)
papers.key_contribution: Method that maps production data from existing manufacturing systems into DPP submodel elements, following the AAS structure, without changing the source systems. Feasibility shown in a real-world use case; the design allows flexible updates of passport content.
papers.conformance_relevance: Generated AAS fits aas.validate. Mapped values (units, ranges, freshness of production data) fit data.rules packs. Update behaviour fits persistence.versions.

papers.title: Am I in Good Shape? Flexible Way to Validate Asset Administration Shell Data Entry via Shapes Constraint Language
papers.venue: IEEE International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Factory Automation (ETFA), 2023 (venue confirmed by OpenAlex)
papers.key_contribution: Stack: SHACL shapes applied to AAS content, used both for schema compliance and for validating data entry; platform independent. Shown in one use case; no scale evaluation is stated.
papers.conformance_relevance: Direct evidence for the acceptance criterion of data.shacl (interface_only): shapes as pinned local files whose verdicts should agree with the JSON Schema path. Complements aas.validate, which wraps aas-test-engines and does not express project-specific constraints.

papers.title: Implementing Level 2 of the ZVEI-Show-Case PCF@Control Cabinet
papers.venue: Unknown Journal (white paper; tool returned no venue or author)
papers.key_contribution: Stack: AAS in multi-level value networks. Sixteen manufacturers of electronic components supplied product and sustainability data as AAS for a control-cabinet demonstrator first built in 2022. The bottom-up approach tested earlier theory in practice and fed findings back to committees; the abstract states no limitations.
papers.conformance_relevance: Multi-tier carbon-footprint exchange gives realistic fixtures: one AAS per supplier for aas.validate. Footprint values are decimals, while canonical bodies in the engine hold no floats, so data.rules would compare decimal strings.
papers.note: No DOI returned by the tool, so no DOI check was possible. Author not returned. Kept because it is one of few multi-company AAS pilots.

papers.title: Product Digital Twin Ontology: A Pivot for Bridging Asset Administration Shell-based and Ontology-based Digital Product Passports.
papers.key_contribution: An ontology (PDTO) plus a method that converts between AAS-based DPPs (using the ECLASS vocabulary) and ontology-based DPPs. The abstract states no evaluation results.
papers.classification_scheme: Distinguishes two families of DPP representation: AAS with ECLASS (industrial, template driven) and ontology or knowledge-graph based (open, distributed, knowledge centric).
papers.conformance_relevance: Two representations of one passport imply an equivalence test (round trip AAS to RDF and back). No existing check does this; it would be a new capability with a pinned mapping. data.shacl (interface_only) would validate the RDF side.

papers.title: A General-Purpose Tool to Convert Asset Administration Shell Templates to RDFS/OWL
papers.key_contribution: Software that converts AAS templates (version 3.0 of the metamodel) into RDFS and OWL, applied to the Battery Pass and CarbonFootprint models. Semantic Treehouse tooling consumed the output to show model reuse; no scale evaluation is stated.
papers.conformance_relevance: Shows that open IDTA templates and the Battery Pass model can be turned into machine-readable constraints, which could feed pinned shapes for data.shacl (interface_only). Also a route to derive data.context vocabularies.

papers.title: RePlanIT Ontology for Digital Product Passports of ICT: Laptops and Data Servers
papers.key_contribution: Stack: ontology and knowledge graph for ICT hardware, components, materials and circular-economy concepts, built from a literature survey, interviews and expert input. Ontology and graph were validated in a real government ICT-procurement case.
papers.classification_scheme: Ontology levels: ICT device, hardware components, materials, circular economy.
papers.conformance_relevance: A sector ontology can be pinned as an allowed context for data.context. Graph conformance would use data.shacl (interface_only).

papers.title: From Conceptual Silos to a Circular Economy: The BFO-Based Framework for the Digital Product Passport
papers.key_contribution: Critical analysis of the CIRPASS-2 Core Ontology that finds ambiguities, for example a mix of physical processes and digital instructions, and proposes a refined framework grounded in Basic Formal Ontology. Evaluation is analytic; no runtime test is stated.
papers.conformance_relevance: Warns that the official core ontology may change. The engine should pin ontology versions and record them in the IXIT, and treat context allowlists (data.context) as versioned inputs.

papers.title: Design and Implementation of a Digital Product Passport Prototype for a Coffee Machine in the Circular Economy
papers.venue: Zenodo repository record (OpenAlex type: article; not shown to be peer reviewed)
papers.key_contribution: Stack: FastAPI backend with information-specific endpoints, a JSON-LD data format and a web interface, for a small appliance. The authors report that the data model covers the identified use cases and gives measurable benefits for material traceability and visibility of product condition.
papers.conformance_relevance: JSON-LD plus per-information endpoints fit data.context, data.jsonschema and api.contract (FastAPI publishes an OpenAPI description that can be pinned). A candidate shape for a local reference system; never call a live copy.

papers.title: ConSolid: A federated ecosystem for heterogeneous multi-stakeholder projects
papers.key_contribution: Stack: Solid pods extended with metadata patterns, microservices, metadata-generated virtual views over an access-controlled SPARQL interface, and a recursive way to discover multi-pod aggregations. Shown with minimal running examples and an architecture-engineering-construction use case; not a DPP system as such.
papers.conformance_relevance: Only Solid-based item found. Pod access control is not modelled by access.restricted_fields; a loopback Solid pod fixture and a pod-access probe would be new. Relevant to construction passports only by analogy.
papers.note: OpenAlex gives publication date 2023-06-09; the search tool gave 2024 (probably the issue year). The 2023 date is used.

papers.title: Empowering End-of-Life Vehicle Decision Making with Cross-Company Data Exchange and Data Sovereignty via Catena-X
papers.key_contribution: Stack: a decision-support application on Digital Twin data inside the Catena-X data space, using Gaia-X principles for contract negotiation and usage policies. Built with user-centred design, the V-model and a scaled agile method, and validated with an end-of-life vehicle use case.
papers.conformance_relevance: Data flows through connectors that a black-box engine cannot see. No existing check applies; a new capability would be a dataspace connector mock (catalogue, negotiation, transfer) on loopback.

papers.title: Usage Policies for Fragmented Digital Product Passport Data Retrieval in AECO Data Spaces
papers.key_contribution: Stack: proof-of-concept data space on Eclipse components with asset registration, usage policy definition, contract negotiation and authenticated retrieval. Demonstrated with a suspended ceiling element offered by several providers under different policies; authors describe it as the first technical validation of decentralised DPP exchange in construction.
papers.conformance_relevance: Policy-driven exposure per consumer is the dataspace analogue of access.restricted_fields, but that check probes roles over HTTP, not negotiated contracts. New capability: connector mock with policy fixtures.
papers.note: Author order conflict: the search tool lists Ekaterina Petrova first; OpenAlex lists Krista van Zandwijk first (4 authors). Not resolved.

papers.title: Digital Product Passport Data Transfer via Dataspace Connector: Technical Implementation and Analysis
papers.venue: 2025 29th International Conference on System Theory, Control and Computing (ICSTCC)
papers.key_contribution: Stack: Eclipse Dataspace Connector prototype exchanging structured product data between economic operators under pre-negotiated contracts with HTTP push. Shows data sovereignty and contract-based governance; the authors state the scope is limited and excludes identity frameworks and regulatory integration.
papers.conformance_relevance: Push transfer means the engine would need a receiving endpoint; a passive pull engine cannot observe it. New capability: loopback connector mock with a transfer-process state check. The OpenAPI client for EDC in prior sources can seed the contract.

papers.title: Battery Passport Generation Method Based on Trusted Data Space
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 7th International Conference on Computer Information and Big Data Applications
papers.key_contribution: Stack: industrial internet identity resolution for addressing, the SM9 algorithm for encryption and signatures, JSON and TypeScript as light contract description languages, and a self-developed data interaction connector. The abstract reports no measured evaluation.
papers.conformance_relevance: A signature algorithm outside the engine allowlist would give unsupported, not pass, under integrity.jws (honest-state rule). Programmable contract languages are outside any current check.

papers.title: Bridging the Gaps Towards a Unified Architecture for Digital Product Passports: A Data Space Perspective on Existing Standards and Initiatives
papers.key_contribution: Layered blueprint that combines data spaces (connectors, identity and trust, federated catalogues, policy contracts), AAS for product data structure, CIRPASS semantic models for shared vocabularies, and GS1 for identifiers and event semantics. Conceptual; no evaluation stated.
papers.classification_scheme: Four layers: data space (governance and infrastructure), AAS (structure of product data), semantic models (vocabularies and ontologies), GS1 (identification and event semantics).
papers.conformance_relevance: Gives a layer model for mapping engine capabilities: identification (identifier.*), semantics (data.context, data.shacl), structure (aas.validate, data.jsonschema), data space (no check today).

papers.title: Digital Product Passport Management with Decentralised Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials
papers.key_contribution: The authors derive nine requirements from the Ecodesign Regulation (as they read it): product identification, passport granularity, who maintains the passport over time, availability that may outlast the maker, who may write, role-based access, authenticity and immutability, security and privacy, and low burden. They map these to DIDs and VCs without fixing a DID method, credential format or software stack. Despite the abstract, there are no measured benchmarks: evaluation is a cost estimate on a public DID ledger (June 2024 token prices) plus illustrative use cases.
papers.limitations_reported: Access-control design waits for delegated acts; resolving a product with many parts may need many ledger reads; a revocation-based design makes the manufacturer a trusted party; ownership history raises privacy concerns; wallet interoperability is fragmented; use cases are illustrative, not empirically validated.
papers.classification_scheme: Two design proposals compared: one DID per product (traceable, costlier) and credentials only with status-list revocation (cheaper, trusts the manufacturer).
papers.conformance_relevance: JWS-secured credentials can be checked with integrity.jws (signature, issuer trust, certificate validity as separate findings). Credential status is integrity.status_list (interface_only); DID resolution would be a new mock-only capability. Legal readings in this paper are secondary_only; cite the Regulation. The paper names an ISO/IEC identification standard as an anchor; its content is not described here.
papers.content_read: full text, body read (arXiv HTML v1, first 100,000 of 116,235 characters); references not read

papers.title: Enhancing Digital Product Passports with Material Fingerprinting and Decentralized Non-Conformity Signals: Application to Critical Raw Materials
papers.key_contribution: Architecture and data model from the Ma-DiTraCe project: self-sovereign identity and verifiable credentials, material fingerprints (chemical, isotopic, spectral) issued as signed credentials to tie physical material to the passport, a decentralised 'red flag' mechanism aggregating non-conformity signals, and optional blockchain anchoring. No evaluation stated in the abstract.
papers.conformance_relevance: Issuer signatures: integrity.jws. Revocation or red-flag state: integrity.status_list (interface_only). The physical-to-digital binding cannot be tested remotely and needs manual.review.

papers.title: COBALT-P - Offene Kreislaufwirtschaftsplattform für optimierte Lebenszyklen und den prädiktiven Handel von Batterien; Teilprojekt: Entwicklung eines sicheren Datenaustauschs und Weitergabe von Batterieinformationen für eine dezentrale Plattform auf Basis von Blockchain und digitalen Zwilling
papers.venue: RENATE repository, OpenAlex type: report (project report)
papers.key_contribution: German-language project report. A technology partner built a DID-based digital battery passport service: a decentralised-identifier method, a stack to issue and verify verifiable credentials, a schema management service, and integration into a battery marketplace used as demonstration environment.
papers.conformance_relevance: Versioned schema service maps to data.jsonschema with pinned schemas. Credential verification maps partly to integrity.jws. Marketplace integration is not testable from outside.

papers.title: Human-Centric Digital Product Passports: Enabling Verifiable Information Sharing for Sustainable Consumption through Wallet-Based Identity Management and Zero-Knowledge Proofs
papers.venue: Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS) proceedings (confirmed by OpenAlex)
papers.key_contribution: Textile DPP prototype with wallet-based identities, non-fungible tokens and zero-knowledge proofs so that consumers receive verifiable information while supply-chain actors keep sensitive data private. A sample infrastructure; no quantitative evaluation in the abstract.
papers.conformance_relevance: Zero-knowledge proof verification is not supported by any engine check; verdicts must be unsupported, not pass. Selective disclosure is the failure mode that access.restricted_fields probes from the plain HTTP side only.

papers.title: Compliance-by-Design: Validating Decentralised Architectures for Digital Product Passports under the EU Data Governance Act
papers.venue: 2025 21st International Conference on Network and Service Management (CNSM)
papers.key_contribution: Assesses a decentralised DPP architecture (data intermediaries, decentralised identity, cryptographic mechanisms) against the Data Governance Act, with GDPR and ESPR as secondary lenses. Early pilots in two projects (PACEDPP, USEFLEDS) serve as empirical validation.
papers.classification_scheme: Requirement lenses: neutrality, structural separation, fair access, registration, confidentiality (as named in the abstract).
papers.conformance_relevance: Template for tying architecture claims to legal criteria in an ICS. Most criteria (neutrality, structural separation) are organisational and fit manual.review, not automated checks. Statements about what the Act requires must cite the Regulation itself, not this paper.

papers.title: Blockchain-based digital product passport: design principles and demonstration
papers.key_contribution: Two-year design-science project producing an end-to-end blockchain DPP prototype for the textile supply chain, covering upstream transformation traceability and downstream events. Defines the information flow over the life cycle and proposes eleven design principles; the abstract reports suitability, not measured performance.
papers.conformance_relevance: Ledger anchoring has no existing check. A new capability would verify a recorded inclusion proof offline; the engine must never call a node. Event history fits persistence.versions.

papers.title: Digital Product Passport Implementation Based on Multi-Blockchain Approach with Decentralized Identifier Provider
papers.key_contribution: Stack: Hyperledger Fabric network for passport data plus decentralised identifiers on a public identity platform. Data model with Product, Manufacturer, Supplier and Material entities; performance tests of create-read-update-delete operations and scalability. Client applications and wider scaling tests are left to future work.
papers.conformance_relevance: Entity-relation data model can be a data.jsonschema fixture. The DID layer has no check. Latency figures from a lab network should not become engine thresholds.

papers.title: A Sustainable Product Tracking System under the Combination of Textile Label Regulations and Digital Product Passport
papers.key_contribution: Stack: Hyperledger Fabric prototype that links textile labelling data with DPP records. An end-to-end run on an organic cotton garment gave about 3.2 s transaction latency and more than 45 transactions per second; the authors claim immutable tracking against greenwashing.
papers.conformance_relevance: Label fields (fibre composition, origin) are static attributes checkable by data.rules completeness; chain integrity has no check.

papers.title: Using composable NFTs and blockchain for the creation of EV battery digital passports with sustainability and traceability features
papers.key_contribution: Stack: composable non-fungible tokens and smart contracts with off-chain storage, giving component-level provenance for EV batteries. Tested in a simulated environment with a sustainability score across four cathode chemistries and ten indicators, plus cost and security analysis. Stated limitations: simulation-only validation, no stakeholder testing, scalability in live deployments; contract code is public.
papers.conformance_relevance: Typical limitation set (simulation, no stakeholders) shows why a black-box conformance suite adds value. Off-chain data fits data.* checks; token state has no check.

papers.title: Demonstration of a Digital Product Passport System for Second-Hand Electronic Devices
papers.key_contribution: Open-source DPP system for the lifecycle of second-hand computers, aimed at repairers, refurbishers and customers, with a blockchain-based registry for trust. Deployable as microservices; the authors note that most commercial DPP systems are proprietary, which blocks research.
papers.conformance_relevance: A deployable open-source system could run on loopback as a reference target. Its registry record maps to registry.consistency against a mock registry (no real chain call).

papers.title: LLM-based JSON mapping and blockchain integration for Digital Product Passports
papers.key_contribution: Pipeline that maps raw sensor data to a standard JSON form with large language models and stores records on a blockchain through smart contracts. Proprietary models were more accurate than open-weight ones; direct prompts beat prompts that generate transformation functions; structured output kept schema validity but introduced wrong values.
papers.conformance_relevance: Schema validity does not imply correct values, so data.jsonschema alone is insufficient and data.rules plausibility checks matter. The engine itself must not use a language model at run time (repository rule 4); this paper is subject matter and a source of test data only.
papers.note: OpenAlex capitalises the title differently (JSON Mapping and Blockchain Integration); otherwise identical.

papers.title: Building Digital Product Passports: EPCIS 2.0 Meets Knowledge Graphs
papers.key_contribution: Architecture that links EPCIS 2.0 visibility events through GS1 keys into a knowledge graph, so one query returns the full history across transformations and aggregations; events are ingested in real time from distributed sources. Evaluation figures are not in the abstract.
papers.conformance_relevance: EPCIS 2.0 JSON documents could be checked with data.jsonschema if the schema is pinned. Lineage consistency (aggregation and transformation chains) has no check; it would be a new event-lineage capability.

papers.title: A DLT- and ZKP-Enabled Framework for Privacy-Preserving Digital Product Passports in Maritime Container Logistics
papers.key_contribution: Stack: GS1 EPCIS 2.0, oneM2M, IOTA anchoring with Merkle batching, and Groth16 zero-knowledge proofs. Sixteen single-host experiments with synthetic load: 95th-percentile latency 48 ms without proofs and 500 ms with, 7 events/s per host, proof generation 304 ms and verification 9.8 ms on average, no permanent message loss in four failure-injection scenarios. Authors state multi-host and public-network validation is future work.
papers.conformance_relevance: The failure-injection scenarios are a test-design pattern for availability and loss checks (persistence.scheduled, interface_only). How the paper measured EPCIS compliance is not stated in the abstract. Anchor and proof checks have no existing capability.

papers.title: Made2Verify: A Scalable GS1-Compliant Resolver and Fallback Dashboard for Digital Product Passports
papers.key_contribution: Resolver and fallback dashboard between physical identifiers (QR, NFC) and passport repositories, built on GS1 standards. It redirects by lifecycle stage, authentication need and endpoint availability, and keeps information reachable if a manufacturer stops operating. Tested with a remanufacture reference part in a lab and a production environment.
papers.conformance_relevance: identifier.resolve is bounded resolution and identifier.parse accepts only /01/<GTIN>/21/<serial>, so lifecycle-aware redirects and fallback cannot be judged today; persistence.scheduled (interface_only) would be needed for availability over time. NFC input maps to carrier.nfc (interface_only).

papers.title: How the Digital Product Passport Can Lead the Plastics Industry towards a Circular Economy—A Case Study from Bottle Caps to Frisbees
papers.key_contribution: Pilot recycling run: 2192 frisbees made from collected bottle caps (486.7 kg of feedstock became 363.2 kg of product) with traceability through all process steps in a one-layer, GS1-based passport from the R-Cycle initiative. Needed an agreed dataset and extra data work; the one-layer design is public but cannot carry sensitive data, and may not suit small simple items.
papers.classification_scheme: Passport depth: one layer (open to all) versus layered access (not provided here).
papers.conformance_relevance: Mass balance between input and output is a relationship rule for data.rules. A public one-layer passport makes access.restricted_fields trivial (all paths public).

papers.title: STVgoDigital: A Digital Product Passport Solution
papers.venue: Communications in Computer and Information Science
papers.key_contribution: Portuguese project (PPS1) implementing traceability for textile and clothing products as a candidate DPP solution. The abstract reports project results in general terms; stack and evaluation details are not given.
papers.conformance_relevance: Evidence that national textile pilots exist; the abstract is too thin to derive checks. See Rosado da Cruz (2024) below for the data-validation follow-up from the same sector.
papers.note: First-author conflict: SciSpace lists Maria João Nabais Sá first; OpenAlex lists Miguel Sá first (12 authors). Not resolved.

papers.title: A framework for evaluating the traceability of primary data elements for textile digital product passports
papers.key_contribution: A Traceability Degree Score for primary data elements, rated on five-point maturity scales over four dimensions. Tested on a man-made cellulosic fibre textile with 336 data elements across 10 supply-chain nodes: only 20% scored top traceability and about 5% scored poorly, mostly in use and end-of-life stages.
papers.classification_scheme: Four traceability dimensions: data standardisation, process automation, measurement reliability, blockchain readiness; each on a five-point maturity scale.
papers.conformance_relevance: An evaluation method for how well a data element ties to the physical product. No check measures this; the link is a manual.review item. Freshness and completeness per lifecycle stage fit data.rules.

papers.title: Data Quality Assessment for the Textile and Clothing Value-Chain Digital Product Passport
papers.venue: International Conference on Enterprise Information Systems (confirmed by OpenAlex)
papers.key_contribution: A software service that validates values of the metrics traced across the textile value chain and integrates with the passport, plus an admin platform to configure rules per metric. Motivated by companies at different digital maturity, some entering data by hand.
papers.conformance_relevance: Same idea as data.rules packs (per-metric units, ranges, completeness). A mature rule pack format could borrow its per-metric configuration model.
papers.note: First-author conflict: the search tool lists A. M. Rosado da Cruz first; OpenAlex lists Adriana Cruz first (6 authors). Not resolved.

papers.title: Material passport for modular construction
papers.key_contribution: Testbed built in Unity on a 3D BIM model of a modular house, with user stories and data requirements gathered from six UK stakeholders. Each building component carries a unique product ID for traceability and quality assurance; the authors aim for up to 30% less waste in the long term (an aspiration, not a measured result).
papers.conformance_relevance: BIM-native data is not JSON, so no check applies unless exported. The unique component ID relates to identifier.consistency; physical tagging relates to carrier.* checks.

papers.title: Current methodologies of creating Material Passports: A Systematic Literature Review
papers.key_contribution: Systematic review (Kitchenham guidance with PRISMA steps): 549 records reduced to 33, 40 after snowballing. Finds that passports are mostly static, need manual input and lack real-time updates, and proposes dynamic passports with automated collection.
papers.classification_scheme: Approaches to creating material passports: BIM-based, blockchain-based, platform-based, QR code or RFID based, Level(s)-based (the abstract counts six approaches but names five).
papers.conformance_relevance: Static versus dynamic passports matters for persistence.versions (update rule). The carrier approaches (QR, RFID) relate to carrier.qr_decode today and carrier.rfid (interface_only).
papers.note: OpenAlex writes the title in sentence case (material passports, systematic literature review); words identical.

papers.title: Integrating BIM, Virtual Reality, and Material Passports for Early-Stage Circular and Low-Carbon Material Selection
papers.key_contribution: Four-layer framework (data, passport, interaction, decision) implemented as a proof of concept in a classroom fit-out case; BIM objects link to passport records with embodied carbon, reuse and disassembly data. Compared with a plain BIM workflow on decision time, confidence, understanding, usability and selection quality; barriers are interoperability, data consistency, standardisation and ownership.
papers.conformance_relevance: User-experience measures are outside the engine. Passport record fields (embodied carbon, lifespan) fit data.rules range checks.

papers.title: End of life focused data model for a digital battery passport
papers.key_contribution: Data needs of recyclers drawn from interviews with eight experts; most data exist but dynamic and use-phase data have gaps. Needs and provision were grouped into a data model, which was used to set up a prototype battery passport platform.
papers.conformance_relevance: Dynamic fields such as state of health need freshness rules in data.rules and version observation in persistence.versions. Statements about legal data requirements must cite Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, not this paper.

papers.title: Battery Passport
papers.key_contribution: The returned text, which begins mid-sentence, describes how pilots of a first battery-passport proof of concept (Global Battery Alliance vision) were configured, what was learned, and next steps. The DOI is book level, so the text may be a chapter abstract; see anomalies.
papers.conformance_relevance: Pilot learnings are a source of requirements, but the excerpt holds no technical detail; do not cite specifics until the chapter is read.
papers.note: Title and DOI match a book-level OpenAlex record. Whether the excerpt belongs to this book is unverified.

papers.title: BatteryPass-12K: The First Dataset for the Novel Digital Battery Passport Conformance Task
papers.key_contribution: Public benchmark of 12,000 passports (CC-BY-4.0, Hugging Face; test split withheld), built from battery passports of Global Battery Alliance pilots (six of ten checked pilots exposed all ten public fields). Variants were generated and judged with language models, with human review of 200 samples, and half are labelled conformant. Nonconformant here means internally inconsistent in one of six ways: inconsistent linked values, unrealistic entries, physical amounts that conflict with traced amounts, conflicting dates, invalid codes, wrong array lengths; labels do not measure full regulatory compliance. Twenty-two models were tested zero-shot (best F1 0.98 on validation, 0.71 on test) and prompt injection lowered scores.
papers.limitations_reported: Only ten fields, few producers behind the pilots, synthetic samples, English and EU rules only, and nonconformance defined as inconsistency only.
papers.classification_scheme: Six defect classes for internal consistency of a battery passport (listed above).
papers.conformance_relevance: The six defect classes map onto data.rules (relationships, ranges, dates, code lists, array lengths) and could seed a fault list; validation/fault-catalogue.yaml is a protected file, so any change is an owner decision (not edited). The engine cannot use language models (rule 4); synthetic samples must be labelled synthetic and are not evidence about real systems. The pilot passports sit at public URLs; none was called here (rule D). Injection results support treating SUT text as data (rule 8).

papers.title: Digital Product Passport Design Supporting the Circular Economy Based on the Asset Administration Shell
papers.key_contribution: DPP data model built on AAS: standards and literature consolidated, data requirements mapped to IDTA submodel templates, and gaps filled where templates lack data. Presented as specific enough for uses such as the EU battery passport yet cross-industry; no runtime evaluation stated.
papers.conformance_relevance: Template-based models can be checked with aas.validate; completeness against regulated attribute lists (Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 Annex XIII) fits data.rules. The gap list is a source of expected-missing fields.
papers.note: OpenAlex lists the first author as M. Kuhn; the search tool gave Maximilian Kühn.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Review of Digital Product Passports in Sustainable Manufacturing: Current State, Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.key_contribution: Systematic review of 225 peer-reviewed studies. The field is mostly conceptual with little empirical validation; blockchain is the most proposed enabler but raises scale, cost and energy concerns, which points to hybrid architectures. Proposes a lifecycle framework based on information inheritance.
papers.classification_scheme: More than twenty attributes per study, including study type, sector, data and information modelling, architecture, technology stack, governance, scalability and sustainability impact; plus a lifecycle framework in which information is inherited from components and processes to products and materials.
papers.conformance_relevance: Confirms there is little validated evidence to base conformance criteria on. Information inheritance suggests relationship rules between component and product passports in data.rules.

papers.title: Digital Product Passports: A Systematic Literature Review on Framework Design and Validation
papers.key_contribution: Review of frameworks (Scopus and IEEE Xplore) that rates design elaboration and validation maturity. Most are conceptual or architectural; validation is mostly illustrative cases, stakeholder assessments or prototypes, and few studies test scalability, interoperability or lifecycle operation.
papers.classification_scheme: Framework archetypes: data-centric, layered, technology-anchored, ecosystem-oriented. Validation maturity: illustrative case, stakeholder-informed assessment, prototype (few beyond).
papers.conformance_relevance: Supplies the validation-maturity ladder to describe what a conformance report adds. Named gaps (cross-organisational testing, shared reference architectures) are the gaps the engine targets.

papers.title: Enabling a dynamic information flow in digital product passports during product use phase: A literature review and proposed framework
papers.key_contribution: Review of 25 DPP frameworks across industries. QR codes and RFID are the common data carriers in manufacturing and construction, and blockchain is the most used security measure; updates by third parties during the use phase are rarely supported. Proposes a conceptual blockchain framework for verified users to update passports.
papers.classification_scheme: Four areas examined per framework: data carrier, data source, data security, user access and verification; passport content sorted into four lifecycle stages.
papers.conformance_relevance: The four areas map onto engine checks: carrier.*, data.*, integrity.*, access.restricted_fields. Third-party updates during use mean persistence.versions needs to handle changes by several writers.

papers.title: Exploring the Design Space and Research Directions for Digital Product Passport Systems
papers.venue: 2025 21st International Conference on Network and Service Management (CNSM)
papers.key_contribution: Identifies three technical dimensions of a DPP system and lists architectural options and open problems for each (counterfeiting, interoperability, data sovereignty); calls for research on decentralised identity and granular access management.
papers.classification_scheme: Three dimensions: data carrier; online storage for product information; updating of dynamic data.
papers.conformance_relevance: Dimensions align with carrier.*, identifier.* plus data.*, and persistence.versions. Counterfeiting is physical authenticity, which digital consistency checks cannot prove.
papers.note: The search tool spells the first author Kaser; OpenAlex spells it Käser.

papers.title: Under The Industrial Hood: A Taxonomy for Digital Product Passports
papers.first_author: Ahmad Iqbal Bin Mohd Shahir Shamsir
papers.venue: Gesellschaft für Informatik (conference paper per DataCite and OpenAlex)
papers.key_contribution: Taxonomy of DPP implementations derived from 32 academic papers and 50 real-world use cases, intended to harmonise understanding and help users configure passports. The full text is only available on request, so the dimensions were not read.
papers.classification_scheme: A taxonomy; its dimensions and classes are not in the abstract, and the full text was not accessible (publisher page offers 'request a copy'; the Fraunhofer repository page was behind bot protection and was not bypassed).
papers.conformance_relevance: Candidate source for ICS profile dimensions. Not usable until the dimensions are read from the full text.
papers.note: SciSpace listed only Frederik Moller as author; DataCite and the GI repository list three authors, first Shamsir, then Paeplow, then Möller. Crossref returned 404 for this DOI; DataCite and OpenAlex resolve it.

papers.title: Legal Challenges and Technical Solutions to Decentralised Digital Product Passports
papers.venue: Gesellschaft für Informatik (conference paper per DataCite and OpenAlex)
papers.key_contribution: Reads the Ecodesign Regulation as favouring decentralisation and analyses it at three levels: minting of unique identifiers, data storage, and distributed storage of passport information. Concludes that distributed storage is legally and operationally problematic. Legal statements here are the authors' reading; tag secondary_only.
papers.classification_scheme: Three decentralisation levels: unique identifier minting; data storage; distributed storage of DPP information.
papers.conformance_relevance: Identifies where the identifier is minted and who stores data, which decides whether identifier.consistency and registry.consistency are meaningful for a given SUT. Cite the Regulation, not this paper, for any legal requirement.
papers.note: Crossref returned 404 for this DOI; DataCite and OpenAlex resolve it with the same title.

cross_paper_observations: Most prototypes are single-site demonstrators or lab testbeds. Two reviews (Psarommatis 2026, Lyse 2026) independently report that conceptual and framework papers dominate and that validation beyond illustrative cases is rare.

No paper found reports running a conformance suite against a DPP system. The nearest items are SHACL validation of AAS content (Rimaz 2023), validation of an architecture against a regulation through pilots (Fabianek 2025), and a conformance-labelled dataset whose labels mean internal consistency only (Adewumi 2026).

Stacks cluster by method family: AAS with REST and role-based access; data spaces with Eclipse Dataspace Connector and contract negotiation; permissioned ledgers (Hyperledger Fabric) with off-chain data; DID and verifiable credentials for issuer identity and roles; knowledge graphs for query; EPCIS 2.0 for events; a GS1-based resolver for access from a carrier.

Hybrids are the norm, not the exception: AAS inside a Gaia-X service (Gleich 2024), a four-layer blueprint (Kranner 2026), EPCIS with ledger and zero-knowledge proofs (Khairy 2026), Fabric with DIDs (Hulea 2024), AAS templates converted to RDF (Kuiper 2026).

Reported performance numbers come from single-host or lab networks (Khairy 2026, Zhao 2026, Hulea 2024). They do not transfer to a black-box engine, which should record timings as observations and not as pass or fail thresholds.
The limitations authors state repeat: simulation-only validation, no stakeholder testing, scalability unproven, interoperability across organisations untested, and unreliable data at the source.

Valid is not correct. A schema-valid record can hold wrong values (Rohrschneider 2026). The only dataset with a conformance label defines it as internal consistency in six defect classes (Adewumi 2026). Textile work builds separate validation services for metric values (Rosado da Cruz 2024) and scores per-element traceability (Dzidzienyo 2026). This supports layering data.rules above data.jsonschema.

Abstracts can overstate evidence. The abstract of Illán García 2024 promises a performance assessment, but the full text holds a cost estimate and illustrative use cases only. Any claim recorded from an abstract alone should be treated as unverified.

The identifier and carrier layer is thinly tested. Only one resolver prototype with lifecycle-aware redirect and fallback was found (Howie 2026) and one GS1-based pilot (Rumetshofer 2024). No paper tests resolver behaviour against a published resolver standard.

Semantic work is diverging: AAS with ECLASS versus ontology and knowledge-graph DPPs (Nguyen 2026), with converters in both directions (Kuiper 2026) and a critique of the CIRPASS-2 core ontology (Tüzün 2026). Equivalence between representations is an untested area.

Battery passports appear mostly as architectures, data models and proofs of concept (Ott 2024, Niu 2026, COBALT-P 2026, Kühn 2025). No published conformance result for a deployed battery passport was found; the Global Battery Alliance pilots are the only real passports cited as data (Adewumi 2026).

Access control shows up as role-based rules (Pourjafarian 2023), policy contracts in data spaces (Petrova 2026), zero-knowledge selective disclosure (Babel 2025, Khairy 2026) and credentials (Abdallah 2026). The engine's access check covers only HTTP-visible fields per role; the others need new capabilities, mock-only.
Several 2026 items have zero or one citation and appear in conference or proceedings series with limited peer review. Treat them as leads, not settled evidence.
anomalies: OpenAlex via WebFetch: every API response read carried a notice asking an AI agent to register an API key for the user's email address. It is page data, not an instruction from the user, and was not followed. The WebFetch summariser flagged it each time.

SciSpace returned a Zenodo software release titled 'hadijannat/idta-submodel-editor: 1.0.0 - Dataspace Connectivity' (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18374723), listing the repository owner and 'Claude' as authors. It is the owner's own software, not a paper, and is not listed in papers. It concerns AAS submodel tooling with Catena-X/Manufacturing-X onboarding, a BaSyx plus digital twin registry publication path and EDC workflows.

The Solid-pod query returned the 2016 Solid platform papers and general pod studies, not DPP prototypes. The only Solid-based item in scope is ConSolid (construction, not a DPP). No peer-reviewed Solid-pod product passport prototype was found.

The GS1 Digital Link query on SciSpace returned patents and QR-plus-blockchain authenticity papers, not a Digital Link implementation. The GS1-based items (Howie 2026, Rumetshofer 2024) came from other queries.

Duplicate records with different DOIs: Abreu 2025 (IJPR plus two figshare DOIs 10.6084/m9.figshare.28423532 and .v1); Kroell 2026 (Zenodo ...18433712 and ...18433713); Mazzocca survey (arXiv 10.48550/arxiv.2402.02455 and journal 10.1109/comst.2025.3543197); Hassini battery passport paper (preprints.org 10.20944/preprints202401.2152.v1 and Batteries 10.3390/batteries10050153); Harutyunyan auditable PPR framework (Zenodo ...13886348 and ...13886349); several Zenodo copies of one DPP and SSI paper. The canonical journal or first DOI was kept.

Berger 2021 (digital battery passport concept; not listed in papers): Consensus returned the preprint DOI 10.31235/osf.io/e3pmq with the venue Journal of Cleaner Production. OpenAlex resolves that DOI to the journal article 10.1016/j.jclepro.2022.131492 (year 2022). Dropped for scope, not for a title mismatch.

Lin 2026 'Battery Passport' (10.1002/9783527851027) is a book-level record (OpenAlex type: book); the abstract excerpt starts mid-sentence and describes pilot configuration, so it may be a chapter abstract. Recorded with a caution.
The Consensus tool often returned 'Unknown Journal'. Venues are now confirmed by OpenAlex where the paper entry says so; venues that were not re-checked are copied from the search tool.

Author and year conflicts between tools: ConSolid year 2023 (OpenAlex date) versus 2024 (Consensus); Petrova 2026, Sá 2023 and Rosado da Cruz 2024 have different first authors in OpenAlex and in the search tools; SciSpace lists one author for the taxonomy paper where DataCite lists three. First-author fields use the registry value where the registry was unambiguous, otherwise the search-tool value with a note.

Crossref returned 404 for the two Gesellschaft für Informatik DOIs 10.18420/inf2025_141 and 10.18420/inf2025_03; they are registered with DataCite and are known to OpenAlex. A Crossref-only check would have wrongly reported them as not found.

Publisher pages for Elsevier (via linkinghub) returned only a redirect notice, and the Fraunhofer-Publica page returned a bot-protection block (Anubis). No attempt was made to bypass either. The GI repository page offers the taxonomy paper only as 'request a copy'.

Two papers use language models (Rohrschneider 2026, Adewumi 2026). The engine forbids language models at run time (repository rule 4); they are recorded as subject matter and possible data only. BatteryPass-12K points at ten pilot passports published at web URLs; none was called (rule D).
Only the first Consensus server was used; the second (f11045f8...) was not needed. No rate limit was hit. scite, Elicit and Undermind were not used.
truncation: About 70 relevant candidates were retrieved; 47 are recorded. Dropped for scope or overlap: generic SSI/DID surveys and digital health or immunity passports; pre-2020 BIM material passports and 2016 Solid platform papers; patents; the owner's own Zenodo software release; conceptual-only or interview-only papers (for example Canciani 2024, Berger 2023 and 2021, Losa 2025, Jansen 2023, Petrik 2025/2026, Zhang 2024, Lopes 2024, Voulgaridis 2024); and near-duplicates in a family (Plociennik 2022/2024, Reif 2024, Engel 2026, Kunz 2024, Volz 2023, Zink 2026, Manoury 2025, Schmidt 2025, Gallina 2025, Greiner 2024, Nowacki 2023, Alves 2023, Li 2022, Ahn 2023, Tolcha hybrid EPCIS 2025, Seddiqui 2026, Wintercorn 2026, Levesanou 2026, Atta 2021, Qazi 2026, Soavi 2026, Baljon 2025, Cruz 2025). Search result caps: Consensus 20 per call, SciSpace 10 per call, OpenAlex first 25 of 3,541 matches. Content read: abstracts only, except two arXiv papers read in full. The aim of 25 to 45 papers was exceeded by 2 because each method family and the classification reviews needed at least one entry.
